source.title: Chapter 22: Command of the Kayamkulam Frontier

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Dusk going to night. A rocky hill a little inland from the coast, half swallowed by mango trees; near its crown the low gopuram of an old Shiva shrine barely clears the canopy. At the hill's foot, a small party with no banners, no elephants, no palanquin: a handful of Nair guards with torches, a few horses, the riders too small to make out. A narrow stone stair cuts up through the trees.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The king liked to meet his gods without the court watching.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fishermen said this shrine was older than any king brave enough to pretend the coast belonged to him.

panels.description: At the foot of the stair, in torchlight. Marthanda Varma still mounted, in plain temple dress: face from the varma-v1 sheet ONLY, bare-headed with his black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, NO turban, NO peacock crest, NO spear; bare chest, heavier build, cream mundu with a thin gold border, one GOLD chain, pearl drop earrings, a fresh line of sandal paste across the brow. Ramayyan Dalawa at his stirrup, looking up at him, careful and insistent: thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle under his arm.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You remember the festival night, when you fell on the temple stones.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Not every knife announces itself.

panels.description: Varma dismounting, handing his reins to a waiting stable boy without looking at him (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO turban, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest, one gold chain, pearl drop earrings). Behind him, still mounted, the heir: a boy of about ten with wide, watchful eyes, in a small white mundu. At the edge of the torchlight on the right, Nagoji on foot in the Ananthan Pillai look: HIGH topknot on the crown, NO turban, cream mundu, cream shoulder cloth across the chest, SILVER chain of office, small gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin, first grey at the temples, the Goa brand on his left wrist, no forehead mark, lean build. Uninjured: no bandage, no sling. No talwar and no knife: he carries nothing into a god's courtyard.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If a king cannot sit with his god without a wall of men between them, he is already dead.

panels.description: Two-shot. Ramayyan a step closer to Varma (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear), voice lower, not backing down. Behind them the Nair guards study the trees and pretend not to hear.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If you die, so do many of us who had no say in that decision.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: And if the heir dies with you, this kingdom becomes a feast.

panels.description: Wide, one moment. The Nair guards already settled at the foot of the stair with their torches. Varma on the left (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear), turned to Ramayyan. Ramayyan in the middle, caught mid-bow, his head tilted toward Nagoji, who waits at the edge of the torchlight on the right (high topknot, no turban, shoulder cloth, silver chain, moustache, clean chin; uninjured, unarmed).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You will have your men. They will wait here.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Then take Ananthan. If you insist on trusting no one else with your back tonight, at least trust the man who has seen how Europeans strike.

panels.description: Over Nagoji's shoulder: only his high topknot, the edge of his silver chain and his moustached jaw in the foreground. Beyond him, Varma (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO turban, NO crest, bare chest, one gold chain, pearl drop earrings, sandal line on the brow), his eyes level and hard, settling on him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You will walk behind. You will watch the boy. You will speak only if spoken to.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do not bring your Deccan noise into my god's courtyard.

panels.description: Nagoji's face, close: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, first grey at the temples, high topknot, small gold stud, no forehead mark. The corner of the moustache lifts a fraction. Not quite a smile.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That was his permission, given with all the reluctance of a man swallowing medicine.

panels.description: The climb. The narrow stone stair through the trees, torchlight trembling on wet stone. Varma ahead (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear) with the heir (a boy of about ten in a small white mundu) at his side; Nagoji three steps behind (high topknot, shoulder cloth, silver chain; uninjured, unarmed). Varma looks up through the leaves at the bare rock of the hill as he speaks, to no one in particular.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If I breathe too often under carved ceilings, I forget what rain smells like on bare rock.

panels.description: Wide, full width. The inner courtyard from the top of the stair. Small. Stone flags. A low mandapa leading to a dark sanctum doorway hung with wilting jasmine; oil lamps in niches along a lime-washed wall peeling to bare stone. In the centre, one old jackfruit tree, its thick roots pushing up between the stones. Under it, Varma (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear) and the heir (a boy of about ten in a small white mundu) in namaskaram; the boy's palms are pressed together a beat ahead of the king's, his eyes wide open and fixed on the sanctum. By the mandapa, the temple assistant with a torch and a basket of wicks and ghee: a youth of about seventeen, bare-chested, no shoulder cloth, close-cropped hair, no ash on his brow. A dog asleep by the wall.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Without his spear, without his platform, he looked less like a king and more like any other man who had brought his worries to a god.

panels.description: Medium. Varma turning his head toward Nagoji, who is off panel, quiet, the ghost of humour in it, his hand already on the heir's shoulder to guide him toward the sanctum (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, sandal line on the brow, one gold chain). The heir (a boy of about ten in a small white mundu), palms still pressed together, eyes wide open on the dark doorway, not daring to blink.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Wait here. If anyone comes, tell them the king is scolding his god and does not wish to be scolded in return.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji alone under the jackfruit tree, facing us (high topknot, moustache, shoulder cloth, silver chain; uninjured, unarmed). Over his shoulder, Varma (bare-headed, NO crest) and the heir (small white mundu) stooping into the low sanctum doorway, where the old priest (V13 temple priest face) is lighting the evening lamps; inside, faintly, a black lingam marked with ash. Nagoji's eyes are not on the sanctum. They are moving.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Old habit.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Count the exits. The shadows. The people.

panels.description: A strip of four small insets, echoing the counting grid of chapter 1: a bangled wrist disappearing down the outer steps; the temple assistant (the bare-chested youth with close-cropped hair) waiting at the mandapa with his torch; the old priest's hands with ghee and wicks; the dog asleep, one paw twitching in a chase dream.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Everything seemed ordinary.

panels.description: Wide. From the doorway of the side room a younger priest steps into the lamplight. He is the chaver: young, lean and wiry, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, three thick horizontal stripes of ash across his forehead, oiled hair tied back in a tight knot low at the nape, white cloth wrapped cleanly at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder in the temple style, a sacred thread across his chest. In his hands a small brass plate with flowers and a clay lamp. Do NOT use the V13 temple priest face: an ordinary, forgettable face. Every detail of him is correct. His gaze runs past us, fixed on the boy at the sanctum, out of frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Only his eyes were wrong.

panels.description: Letterbox strip across the chaver's eyes and the three ash stripes above them, lit from below by the clay lamp. Clean-shaven. Unblinking.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They were too still.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Devout men have a certain softness around the gaze. This man had burned away every other thought.

panels.description: Two-shot as the chaver passes within arm's length of Nagoji. Nagoji on the right under the tree (high topknot, thick moustache, silver chain; uninjured, unarmed). The chaver on the left (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow, knot at the nape, cloth over his left shoulder), walking left toward the sanctum without looking at him. The brass plate does not rattle. Behind them the niche lamps bend in the breeze, but the flame on his plate burns straight up. Nagoji speaks softly, in Malayalam (lettered in English).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Ayya. The priest is busy. You may have to wait.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I felt the hairs on my arms rise.

panels.description: The chaver (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow, knot at the nape) stops a few paces from the heir (a boy of about ten in a small white mundu), who has turned back at the sanctum threshold, and lifts the brass plate until the lamp's light touches the boy's face. His mouth moves fast and formal. Behind the boy, Varma (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest) is uncurling his hands from prayer, his shoulders tightening. Only these three figures in frame.

copy.speaker: CHAVER
copy.text: ...Eight Houses... vow... chaver... heir...

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Too fast for my Deccan ears.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Whatever the full words, the king understood them.

directions: (Letter as one balloon with faded gaps between the fragments, the way Nagoji hears it.)

panels.description: Large, one third of the page. One instant. The brass plate falling from the chaver's dropped right hand, flowers lifting off it, the clay lamp tipping from it; his left hand coming up from beneath the edge of his cloth with a long dagger, slightly curved, double-edged, held reversed with the point angled back along his own forearm. Between him and the boy, Varma has already stepped across: planted square in the chaver's path, bare chest forward, arms wide to shield the heir (small white mundu) behind him at the sanctum threshold (Varma bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear). In the background by the tree on the right, Nagoji (high topknot, moustache, silver chain; uninjured, unarmed), eyes locked on the chaver, weight already coming off his back foot as he launches.

Shot from behind the chaver's shoulder. His lunge angles past Varma's bare shoulder toward the boy, and the temple assistant (the bare-chested youth, close-cropped hair, no shoulder cloth) throws himself across that line from the mandapa side, torch still in his fist, mouth open in a sound that is half shout, half prayer. The assistant's body hides the blade entirely.

copy.speaker: ASSISTANT
copy.text: Shiva!

panels.description: Small inset, set into the upper left corner of 4.5. Low, in silhouette: the assistant crumpling to the flags, the torch falling from his hand and rolling, spilling light across the stone. We see the fall, never a wound. Only the assistant in this inset.

Nagoji arriving from the right edge of the panel (high topknot, moustache, silver chain; uninjured), his LEFT hand snapping out to clamp the chaver's dagger wrist, his shoulder driving into the man's ribs. The chaver (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow) on the left. In the background, the dog up and bolting, mid-bark.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My body moved before thought caught up.

panels.description: Varma (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest) half turning, one hand hooking the heir (a boy of about ten in a small white mundu) by the shoulder and shoving him back toward the sanctum. The boy stumbles, still staring; the old priest (V13 temple priest face) catches him and hauls him behind a pillar. The struggle is off panel to the right.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yes. Chaver.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The word surfaced with the shock.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had heard of such men in stories.

panels.description: Tight on the struggle. Nagoji on the right (thick moustache, high topknot, silver chain), his LEFT hand locked on the chaver's wrist; the chaver on the left (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow running with sweat, teeth bared); both men's weight braced, the dagger trembling between them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Warriors from the north who whispered oaths before goddesses and swore to die taking down their target.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He was not a large man, but his arm felt like a rope pulled taut.

panels.description: The chaver's elbow slamming into Nagoji's ribs. Nagoji on the right (moustache, silver chain) folding around it, his left hand still on the wrist. The chaver (clean-shaven) on the left.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Men who trained not for survival, but for a single moment of impact.

panels.description: Insert, tight on the hands. Nagoji's LEFT hand, the Goa brand at his wrist, slipping down the chaver's wrist toward the fist but still hooked around it, as the dagger's point scrapes across the heel of his open palm. Show the slip and the fingers still holding, not the cut. No blood.

The blade darting up, now aimed at Varma's throat, Nagoji's left hand still dragging on the chaver's wrist. Varma (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest) in its path, and he is not stepping back. He is stepping in.

Varma inside the dagger's arc (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest, one gold chain): his left hand clamping the chaver's forearm just above Nagoji's LEFT hand, which is still locked on the wrist; his right hand driving stiff-fingered into the chaver's throat in a kalari strike. The king's face is calm and practised. Nagoji at the right edge (moustache, silver chain; left palm cut, no blood shown).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The stories of his youth, fighting his uncles' men in temple courtyards and river fords, had not been exaggerated.

panels.description: The chaver (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow), gagging, snaps his head forward; his forehead cracks into Varma's brow. Varma (bare-headed, NO crest) reels back a step, the line of sandal paste on his forehead smeared and broken. No blood rendered.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For most men, that would have ended the fight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He was not most men.

panels.description: The dagger surging toward the soft flesh under Varma's jaw. Varma recoiling at the left edge (bare-headed, NO crest, sandal paste smeared); the chaver in the middle; Nagoji on the right (moustache, silver chain), his RIGHT hand shooting up to join his LEFT on the chaver's wrist, catching it a hand-span short.

Two-shot, tight. Nagoji on the right (thick moustache, silver chain, high topknot) and the chaver on the left (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow, knot at the nape), arms tangled high around the dagger, faces inches apart, bodies straining against each other. Lamplight from below.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We looked like dancers locked in an awkward embrace.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His breath stank of betel and kanjav, chewed to make a man deaf to the thought of his own death.

panels.description: Close on the chaver's face (clean-shaven, ash stripes smeared). Pupils blown wide, not with terror but with a fierce joy. His voice is torn by the strike to his throat.

copy.speaker: CHAVER
copy.text: For the old houses.

copy.speaker: CHAVER
copy.text: For those he broke.

panels.description: Nagoji on the right (moustache, high topknot) drives his forehead into the cheekbone of the chaver on the left (clean-shaven). Stage it in the snap of both heads, not in injury.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Stars burst behind my eyes.

panels.description: Low angle at floor level: two men's bare feet in the long smear of lamp oil from the fallen clay lamp, the spilled garland's flowers crushed into it. The chaver's heel skids, and Nagoji's foot hooks behind his ankle.
Both men going down together. Nagoji's RIGHT shoulder takes the stone; his face contorts (moustache, topknot, silver chain). The chaver (clean-shaven) falling with him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Something popped. A hot line of pain ran down my arm.

panels.description: Wide, low, at floor level. The dagger skidding away across the flags, spinning once, coming to rest against the foot of a pillar in a pool of niche-lamp light. Nagoji and the chaver, out of focus behind it.

The chaver (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow) has rolled on top of Nagoji, fingers clawing at his face and neck. Nagoji on his back on the flags (moustache, silver chain, right arm hanging useless, left palm cut). The chaver's right hand has searched Nagoji's waist and found nothing, and is balling into a fist drawn back at his throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had carried no blade into a god's courtyard.

panels.description: Varma's foot taking the chaver in the ribs: a kalari kick, heel driving in, the body folding around it. Varma in temple dress (bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest, sandal paste smeared); the chaver clean-shaven with an ash-striped brow.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He kicked not like a courtier, but like a man who had spent hours in bare earth pits, stamping out the patterns kalari masters taught.

panels.description: Foreground: Nagoji crawling across the stone (moustache, silver chain, right arm hanging useless), his LEFT hand, the Goa brand at the wrist, closing around the dagger's hilt at the pillar's foot. Background: lit from floor level by the assistant's fallen torch on the flags, the SHADOW of Varma kneeling on the chaver, one hand fisted in his hair, is thrown large up the lime-washed wall. Only the shadows; the bodies themselves are out of frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Once.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Twice.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The metal felt warm from recent life.

directions: (Letter "Once." and "Twice." as two small separate caption boxes set on the shadow on the wall. Letter the warm-metal caption low, by the hand.)

panels.description: One frozen instant. Nagoji up on one knee on the right (moustache, topknot, silver chain, right arm hanging), the dagger raised in his LEFT hand. Under Varma, the chaver (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow) arched upward toward the point, eyes on the steel, chest thrust at it; Varma's RIGHT shoulder bearing down on that chest (bare-headed, NO crest, sandal paste smeared).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not to escape. So that his death might yet score the king.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment, I feared the dagger would find us all.

panels.description: Insert, tight: Nagoji's LEFT hand and wrist, the Goa brand showing, turning the dagger flat and sideways, away from the rising chest, the edge travelling out of frame. The chaver's throat is outside the frame. No blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then training took over.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Instead of driving the blade straight down, I angled it.

panels.description: The chaver's point of view, looking up: the jackfruit leaves black against a patch of night sky, a few stars, the edge of a lamp's glow. The frame tilted a little and softening at its edges.

copy.speaker: CHAVER (small, fading)
copy.text: For the old...

panels.description: Wide, high angle from inside the tree's canopy. The courtyard afterwards. The chaver's body still on the stones. Varma (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, NO spear) kneeling back from him. Nagoji on his knees (high topknot, silver chain, right arm hanging), the dagger lowered in his left hand, the hand held away from his body. Behind the pillar, the heir (a boy of about ten in a small white mundu) inside the locked arm of the old priest (V13 temple priest face). The dog flattened against the far wall. Nothing moves. No blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a long moment, all I could hear was breath.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My own, ragged. The king's, rough. The heir's, small and fast.

panels.description: Narrow strip. The temple assistant's open hand on the stone, a youth's bare forearm, the fallen torch guttering beside it. The rest of him out of frame.

Two-shot. On the left, Varma easing himself up off the body (temple dress: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, NO spear, bare chest, one gold chain): a cut splitting the sandal paste on his brow, a split and swelling lip, his right shoulder hanging lower than the left. No blood rendered. On the right, Nagoji getting to his feet (moustache, topknot, silver chain), right arm clamped to his side, left hand clenched over the cut palm.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You are hurt.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: So are you.

panels.description: The old priest (V13 temple priest face) shuffling forward, hands shaking. Varma (bare-headed, NO crest, sandal paste split, lip swelling) cuts him off, not unkindly.

copy.speaker: PRIEST
copy.text: Maharaja... forgive... he came as any other...

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Quiet. Fetch water. Clean cloth. And send a boy down to Ramayyan.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Tell him the king has slipped on the temple steps and needs a bandage.

panels.description: Varma and Nagoji sitting under the jackfruit tree, backs against the trunk, the chaver's body a little distance away. Varma on the left (bare-headed, NO crest, bare chest, split lip), testing the word on his lip, his eyes going to the pillar where the heir (small white mundu) peers out. Nagoji on the right (high topknot, silver chain, right arm hanging, left palm cut).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Chaver. From the Kayamkulam frontier, most likely. One of the old Eight Houses that still dream of undoing me.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: He came for the heir. Not for me.

panels.description: Under the tree. The old priest (V13 temple priest face), back with a water pot and clean cloth, kneels to bind Nagoji's cut left palm; the Goa brand shows at Nagoji's wrist. Nagoji on the right (high topknot, silver chain, right arm hanging), looking at the body. Varma on the left (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, bare chest), head tipped back against the bark, a wet cloth pressed to his brow.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He said it was for the old houses.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Men like him are always for something old. They rarely live long enough to see whether the old was worth killing for.

panels.description: Close on Varma (bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, sandal paste split on the brow, swelling lip). He spits to one side. When he speaks again it is the coldest voice the reader has heard from him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If there are any remnants of the Eight Houses still hiding in these hills, I want chavers sent into their courtyards.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: No last cousin with a purse. No temple man willing to whisper for them. Nothing.

panels.description: Two-shot, quieter. Varma on the left (bare-headed, NO crest) turns his head toward Nagoji on the right, wincing. Nagoji (high topknot, silver chain), his left palm freshly wrapped.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You could have stepped aside. I would be lying broken on this stone now, and you would have a clear road north.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did not think. My body moved.

panels.description: Close on Varma (temple dress, bare-headed, NO crest, sandal paste split on the brow, swelling lip), his eyes lowered to Nagoji's freshly wrapped left hand in the near foreground, the Goa brand at the wrist.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Bodies move toward what they trust. Remember that.

panels.description: Wide. Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, plain white cloth) bursting into the courtyard at the top of the stair, two Nair guards with torches behind him. His composed face is tight, his eyes sweeping the scene in one pass: the chaver's body, the assistant, Varma's split brow, Nagoji's hanging right arm, the heir (small white mundu) behind the pillar with the old priest's arm around him. His jaw clenched. Varma, under the tree on the left (bare-headed, NO crest, bare chest), smiles faintly; Nagoji beside him on the right.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Steps. You slipped on the steps.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The gods are clumsy hosts.

panels.description: Wide. Night. A small lamplit room off the fort courtyard. A court physician (an elderly man in plain white, NOT the V13 temple priest face) tying off the last stitch on Varma's brow. Varma seated on the left in his fort-room look: bare-headed with the side knot above his LEFT ear, NO turban, NO peacock crest, NO spear; plain cream mundu, a cream upper cloth draped over his injured right shoulder, one GOLD chain, pearl drop earrings, fresh sandal paste around the stitches, a cup of watered buttermilk beside him. Nagoji seated on the right: high topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, SILVER chain of office, his RIGHT arm bound across his chest, his left palm wrapped. Between them Ramayyan paces tight lines across the small room, a palm-leaf bundle and stylus in his fist.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Later, at the fort.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I count chiefs who murmur. I watch Dutch papers.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I did not know one had sent a chaver after the heir.

panels.description: Varma (fort-room look: bare-headed, NO crest, stitched brow, cream cloth over his right shoulder) not looking up from his cup, which he holds in his left hand.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you had, you would have forbidden me to climb that hill. I would have gone anyway.

panels.description: Ramayyan slapping the palm-leaf bundle down on the low table beside the lamp, the flame jumping, turned to face Varma (bare-headed, NO crest), who is seated beyond the table.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Yes.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: That is why it infuriates me.

panels.description: Ramayyan turning from the table to Nagoji, seated on the right (right arm bound, left palm wrapped, silver chain), the stylus in his hand pointing at him. Behind them, Varma (bare-headed, NO crest, cream cloth over his right shoulder) shifting in his seat.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You took the blade meant for the heir. That buys you more than thanks.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: It confirms something I had been weighing.

panels.description: Varma risen, standing at the open doorway (fort-room look: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, NO crest, cream cloth over his right shoulder), his back half to us, turning his head toward Nagoji in the room. Beyond him, in the torchlit fort courtyard, horses picketed in a long line.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ram worries about the north, and your hills calling. I worry about the Kayamkulam frontier.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I need men whose first instinct, when a dagger appears, is to move toward my chest, and his, not away from it.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the courtyard: Varma's silhouette in the doorway in the near foreground (bare head with the side knot, cloth over his right shoulder, NO crest). Beyond him the lamplit room: Nagoji seated, looking up at him (high topknot, silver chain, right arm bound, left palm wrapped), and Ramayyan by the low table with his palm-leaf bundle.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: So I will give you what I once offered and you once refused.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: A permanent command on the Kayamkulam frontier. Horse that answer to your word.

panels.description: Varma back at the lamp, shot through its flame: the flame soft and large in the foreground, his face beyond it, serious now, the humour gone (fort-room look: bare-headed, NO crest, stitched brow, one gold chain, pearl drop earrings).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you accept, you tie yourself to this kingdom in a way that will be hard to undo.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you later ride north, you will not go as a free blade, but as a man breaking his own oath.

panels.description: Two-shot across the lamp. Nagoji on the right, dry, glancing down at his wrapped left palm (topknot, silver chain, right arm bound). Varma on the left (bare-headed, NO crest, stitched brow) smiling, the split lip making it hurt.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: A chaver in reverse. Sworn to die in one place instead of to kill in another.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Something like that.

panels.description: Ramayyan alone in frame (thin, receding hair, plain white cloth), cutting in quickly, one hand raised, the stylus still in the other.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You do not have to answer now. Decisions made when the smell of iron is still in the nose can feel different when it fades.

panels.description: Nagoji shaking his head (high topknot, silver chain, right arm bound, left palm wrapped). He looks past Ramayyan's raised hand, blurred in the foreground, toward the king, who is off panel.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: No. If I think too long, I will count too many futures and ride in none.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am tired of standing with one foot in each river.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji facing Varma across the lamp: Nagoji on the right (high topknot, silver chain, right arm bound, left palm wrapped), Varma on the left (fort-room look: bare-headed, NO crest, cream cloth over his right shoulder). Through the open doorway behind them, the picketed horses in the torchlit courtyard. Ramayyan at the edge of the frame, very still.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will take your frontier. I will build horse there that answer to this land.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will send word north of what I have chosen.

panels.description: Nagoji from the chest up, his wrapped left hand resting on the silver chain of office, his right arm bound across his chest. Behind him, out of focus, Ramayyan with the palm-leaf bundle held against his chest.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If the Peshwa or his men think me traitor, they can write my name in their own books.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have no space left in mine for their judgments.

panels.description: Insert, tight: Ramayyan's hand and stylus cutting the order into a fresh palm leaf on the low table, lamplight in the new grooves. The marks stay abstract and unreadable.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: So noted.

panels.description: Two-shot, the two cups meeting large in the foreground over the lamp: Varma's left hand and Nagoji's wrapped left hand, both men toasting left-handed. Behind the cups, Varma on the left wincing mid-laugh at his split lip (bare-headed, NO crest, stitched brow); Nagoji on the right (high topknot, silver chain, right arm bound).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: To clumsy gods and fast horses.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: To careful reckonings that keep us alive long enough to regret our choices.

panels.description: Day. The fort courtyard in hard light, horses picketed along the wall. Padmini Amma arriving, her long walking stick planted hard on the flags: in her fifties, grey threading the thick black hair coiled at her nape, simple gold, cotton sari hitched for walking. She looks Nagoji up and down. He stands with his RIGHT arm in a sling across his chest, left palm wrapped (high topknot, NO turban, mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Word of my new command reached Padmini.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: So. You finally decided which current to trust. I hope your horse can swim.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They can. I am less sure about their rider.

panels.description: Wide, full width. A cavalry column riding north along a coastal track under a monsoon-heavy sky, a red standard with a silver conch snapping above it: Maravar light horse and Madurai lancers with tall spears and plain cloth pennons, around a core of turbaned Maratha riders. Nagoji at its head on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat: HIGH topknot, NO turban, NO red sash, mundu hitched for the saddle, shoulder cloth, SILVER chain of office, talwar at his hip, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin. No sling, no bandage; he holds his right shoulder a little stiffly.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some weeks later.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of the temple stone, of the thin line between life and death measured by inches of steel and a man's decision to step in instead of aside.

panels.description: Large, full width, the rest of the page. The column fording a wide river at dusk, water to the horses' knees, the far bank ahead. Nagoji and Kayal mid-stream (topknot, no turban, no sling), facing forward, the current running around them in one direction.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Kayamkulam frontier waited. So did whatever knives the old houses there had honed in the dark.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But for the first time since Goa, I felt not like wreckage caught between currents, but like part of a river that had chosen its course.

directions: (Set the last caption apart, low in the frame, as the chapter's closing line.)
